observations: Photo 0 shows a black Yamaha keyboard with 61 keys, a music stand, and a control panel with buttons, knobs, and a small LCD screen. The brand 'YAMAHA' is visible on the front panel and music stand.
Photo 1 shows a close-up of the right side of the keyboard, including the keys, control panel, and part of the stand. The model number 'PSR-E273' is visible on the lower right of the control panel.

Photo 2 shows a close-up of the left side of the keyboard, with the brand 'YAMAHA' visible on the music stand and control panel. The keys appear slightly worn, with some white keys showing discoloration or dirt.
All photos show the keyboard placed on a metal stand, with a tiled or concrete floor in the background.
The keyboard has no visible damage to the casing, but the keys show minor signs of use, especially on the white keys.

claims.claim: Used as new keyboard. Everything working perfectly.
claims.evidence: Photos show minor wear on white keys and no functional demonstration. No video or audio proof of operation.

risks.risk: Internal components may be faulty or worn despite appearance.
risks.proof: Video clip showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: Keys may be sticky or unresponsive due to unseen damage or dirt.
risks.proof: Close-up video of pressing multiple keys across the keyboard, showing consistent response.

risks.risk: Missing accessories such as power adapter, sustain pedal, or original case.
risks.proof: Photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the keyboard.

proof_requests: Video clip of the keyboard powered on, playing notes, and showing all functions working.
Photo of all included accessories (power adapter, cables, case, etc.).
Close-up photo of the keys showing no sticking or damage.
response.reason: The model is identifiable as Yamaha PSR-E273, but the seller's claim of 'everything working perfectly' cannot be verified from photos alone. There are visible signs of use on the keys, and functional proof is missing. Without video or audio demonstration, the item must be priced as possibly not working, and accessories are unverified.
